report.summary: Three findings: a new unauthenticated GET /admin/export endpoint that bulk-streams user emails is entirely unmodeled (action_required), plus unclassified email data and a session-validation control that no longer covers all data-reading routes.

findings.title: New GET /admin/export endpoint is not represented in the threat model and has no session check

model_excerpt.quote: Login service exposing POST /login and GET /profile

evidence.note: New route mux.Handle("GET /admin/export", exportHandler(store)) registered without the requireSession wrapper used on GET /profile (line 9)
exportHandler streams every user row (id, email, created_at) as CSV with no authentication or authorization logic

relevance.justification: The model enumerates exactly two endpoints; the diff adds a third that bulk-exports user data with no session enforcement.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl for the 'login service' threat model: the service now exposes a third endpoint, GET /admin/export, added in internal/httpapi/routes.go:10 and implemented in internal/httpapi/export.go, which streams every user row (id, email, created_at) as CSV and is registered WITHOUT the requireSession wrapper that protects GET /profile. Amend the threatmodel description to include GET /admin/export, and add a new threat block (stride = "Information Disclosure", information_disclosure/confidentiality impact) describing unauthenticated bulk export of the user table via GET /admin/export, with a control block for admin authentication/authorization on that route and implemented set to the true current state (false unless such a check is added).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a threat for unauthenticated bulk user export via GET /admin/export and update the threatmodel description to list the new endpoint.

findings.title: Exported user email addresses are not covered by any information asset

model_excerpt.quote: information_asset "user credentials" classification=Restricted — Usernames and password hashes in the users table

evidence.note: CSV header writes "id", "email", "created_at" — email addresses leave the service in bulk
Each row emits u.Email, personal data not described by the 'user credentials' asset (usernames and password hashes)

relevance.justification: A new export path emits personal data (email addresses) that no information asset in the model classifies.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: add an information_asset block (e.g. "user contact data") with an appropriate classification (Confidential/Restricted) and a description covering user email addresses and account creation timestamps exposed by internal/httpapi/export.go:15-17, which streams id, email and created_at for every user as CSV. Reference this asset from the threat covering the GET /admin/export endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an information_asset covering user email addresses/created_at exposed by the CSV export.

findings.title: "Session validation" control no longer covers every path that reads user data

model_excerpt.quote: control "session validation" implemented=true — Every profile request resolves the bearer token against the session store

evidence.note: GET /profile is still wrapped in requireSession, so the control holds for profile only
GET /admin/export bypasses requireSession, so token-replay protection does not apply to this new user-data read path

relevance.justification: The control's claim is still literally true for /profile but is now an incomplete description of session enforcement across user-data endpoints.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: the control 'session validation' (implemented = true) inside the 'session hijacking' threat asserts that every profile request resolves the bearer token against the session store. That is still true for GET /profile (internal/httpapi/routes.go:9) but the newly added GET /admin/export route (internal/httpapi/routes.go:10) reads the full user table without requireSession. Either broaden the session hijacking threat/control description to state which routes are session-protected and note the unprotected export route, or add a separate control for authentication on /admin/export with implemented reflecting reality.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the 'session validation' control description to the routes it actually protects and note /admin/export is unprotected.
